exceptions.reason: Asynchronous schema profiling adds one task kind to task responses and event-subscription filters. Existing kinds and their behavior remain unchanged; clients using closed response enums must support the new kind.
exceptions.migration: Regenerate clients from the updated OpenAPI document or add `schema_profiling` to task-kind response enums before enabling profiling requests and subscriptions.
exceptions.changelog_entry: **Breaking (REST clients with closed task-kind enums):** task and event-subscription responses can now contain `schema_profiling`.

exceptions.reason: Class point responses now expose the revision-owning class entity unless callers explicitly request the collection expansion.
exceptions.migration: Use `include=collection` for the expanded, untagged representation.
exceptions.changelog_entry: class point routes return the class entity by default

exceptions.reason: Permission reads and mutations now return revision-owning permission-set representations instead of the prior flattened records and empty mutation responses.
exceptions.migration: Clients must update deserializers for these response shapes.
exceptions.changelog_entry: SQL permission reads return `{collection_id, revision, permissions}`

exceptions.reason: Group membership reads and mutations now return revision-owning membership entities rather than flattened principals or empty mutation responses.
exceptions.migration: Clients must update deserializers for these response shapes.
exceptions.changelog_entry: group member lists return membership entities with an optional nested principal

exceptions.reason: Canonical user and service-account responses use stable identity-scope identifiers and leave mutable provider metadata to expanded list views.
exceptions.migration: Rich metadata remains available from the corresponding untagged list responses.
exceptions.changelog_entry: canonical tagged user and service-account points use stable `identity_scope_id` values

exceptions.reason: Canonical group responses omit synchronization timestamps because those operational fields do not advance the group's resource revision.
exceptions.migration: The fields remain available in untagged group and token lists.
exceptions.changelog_entry: canonical tagged group points omit directory-sync timestamps

exceptions.reason: Canonical user responses omit synchronization timestamps because those operational fields do not advance the user's resource revision.
exceptions.migration: Rich metadata remains available from the corresponding untagged list responses.
exceptions.changelog_entry: canonical tagged user and service-account points use stable `identity_scope_id` values

exceptions.reason: The event-delivery worker lease token is an internal capability and must not be exposed through public API responses.
exceptions.migration: API clients must stop deserializing or depending on this field.
exceptions.changelog_entry: Event-delivery API responses no longer expose the internal `claim_token` worker lease capability

exceptions.reason: Oasdiff 1.16 reports request/response directionality changes for reused tagged-enum components and treats the typed optional TaskID reference as a nullable widening even though those schemas accept the same JSON values as v0.0.9.
exceptions.migration: No client migration is required because the token-resource and remote-invocation `oneOf` variants are schema-identical to v0.0.9 and optional provenance task IDs retain the same integer-or-null representation.
exceptions.changelog_entry: token-resource and remote-invocation `oneOf` variants remain JSON-compatible

exceptions.reason: API confirmation now queues a restore for an isolated migrator-backed executor instead of holding the request open across the destructive transaction.

Credential creation and renewal, local user creation, and restore confirmation now require operation-bound fresh password approval so a stolen bearer token cannot mint durable credentials or replace identity data. Password patches and credential-bearing imports have the same conditional requirement.
exceptions.migration: Update CLI/frontend/SDK flows to obtain a single-use approval

exceptions.reason: System subscriptions have no collection. Their health entries use the same response with a nullable collection_id, represented as optional by the schema generator.
exceptions.changelog_entry: event-delivery health subscription entries now return a nullable

exceptions.reason: Authentication rejects empty passwords and applies the existing 4096-character login bound to plaintext writes. Credential-approval operations embed the same tightened create/update password schemas; those operations remain supported. Oasdiff also reports the import-credentials variant as replaced because its class-relation import schema adds optional directional labels. All operation variants are unchanged, and removing those two optional properties reproduces the baseline class-relation import schema exactly.
exceptions.migration: reset any existing empty-password credentials before upgrading; they cannot log in afterward.
exceptions.changelog_entry: Reject empty plaintext passwords at creation, update, reset, import, and login

exceptions.reason: Interactive sessions deliberately replace legacy human authentication with client-bound, short-lived access and single-use refresh credentials; old server clients are unsupported.
exceptions.migration: Apply the session migration, upgrade all server replicas and frontend/SDK consumers together, clear existing BFF sessions, and sign in again.
